deviations: Volatility 25th/75th percentiles taken over the party-level estimation sample using Stata's _pctile definition (R quantile type 2); the paper says only 'in the sample'.

Separation-of-powers covariate entered as dummies for assembly-elected and parliamentary systems (presidential omitted); ballot rules as closed-list and open-list dummies (non-list omitted); electoral system as plurality and PR dummies (mixed omitted). Covariate set follows the paper text: party size, union/business/religious links, electoral system, ballot rules, logged mean district magnitude, polity, democratic tenure, political system, logged GDP pc, Gini, ethnic fractionalization.
Ethnic party = more than half of expert coders report ethnic/linguistic linkages (ethnic > 0.5). Ideological extremism = extremist2; extremist party evaluated at distance 3, moderate at 0.

Each Table 1 regression uses its own complete cases: 431 parties (75 countries) for the overall and ethnicity models, 430 for the ideology model (one party lacks extremist2). n_obs_table1 reports 431.
notes: Table 1: OLS (fixest) of personal / programmatic on ev_total plus party- and country-level covariates, SEs clustered by country; the reported differences are linear combinations of the coefficients (high minus low volatility = beta*(p75-p25); group differences include the interaction evaluated at p25 or p75), so they do not depend on where the other covariates are held. Table 2: rdrobust, local linear, triangular kernel, mserd bandwidths, cutoff 0, running variable mv_incparty, open-seat sample dlameduck_runs==0; the conventional point estimate is reported.
